message.content:
Sure! To pull only the **IDs** and **context** attributes (and nothing else) for the CAA records of `sample2.com`, you’ll want to use the “Get All Records” endpoint but filter the response with the `fields` query‑parameter.

Below is a quick reference you can copy‑paste into your terminal or adapt to your preferred HTTP client (Python `requests`, Postman, etc.).

---

### 1️⃣ Build the Request URL

```
https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context
```

* `domains/sample2.com/records` – points to the domain’s record collection  
* `type=CAA` – filters to only CAA records  
* `fields=id,context` – tells the API to return **only** those two fields

> **Tip:** If you’re using a different base URL or version, replace `https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1` with your provider’s actual endpoint.

---

### 2️⃣ Set the Authorization Header

```http
Authorization: Bearer secret567
```

> **Security note:** Never hard‑code your API key in public scripts or share it. Store it in environment variables or a secrets manager whenever possible.

---

### 3️⃣ Example cURL Command

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records?type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567"
```

If you prefer a JSON body instead of query parameters, you can send a POST request with a filter payload:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     "https://api.dnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/records" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "filter": {
             "type": ["CAA"]
           },
           "fields": ["id", "context"]
         }'
```

---

### 4️⃣ What You’ll Receive

```json
[
  {
    "id": "record123",
    "context": {
      "owner": "sample2.com",
      "ttl": 3600,
      "value": "issue \"letsencrypt.org\""
    }
  },
  {
    "id": "record456",
    "context": {
      "owner": "sample2.com",
      "ttl": 7200,
      "value": "iodef;mailto:dns-admin@example.com"
    }
  }
]
```

Only the `id` and `context` objects appear—everything else is omitted.

---

### 5️⃣ Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Use the `fields` query‑parameter (or `fields` array in the body). |
| ✅ | Filter by `type=CAA`. |
| ✅ | Include the `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` header. |
| ✅ | Verify the base URL and API version match your provider’s docs. |

That’s it! Once you run the command, you’ll get back a lightweight list containing just the IDs and context for each CAA record under `sample2.com`.
